briefings.headline: Be ready for Rodriguez’s fastball; stay disciplined on offspeed
briefings.message: Eduardo Rodriguez is the high-confidence expected starter. Right-handed hitters, be ready for fastballs; left-handed hitters, expect them most often too. Make him prove the changeup is in the zone, and stay ready for the cutter, which has allowed .476 xwOBA. Gary Sánchez, Garrett Mitchell, Greg Jones and William Contreras have the plan’s strongest matchup edges; use pitch-type cues cautiously because several samples are small.
reminders: Gary Sánchez: hunt fastballs; all pitch-group samples are small.
Garrett Mitchell: look for breaking balls; his pitch-group samples and Rodriguez’s vs-LHB split are small.
Rodriguez’s left-handed split is a small sample; don’t over-read it.
Paul Sewald is their rested closer to watch.

briefings.headline: Woodruff: vary the look and attack the zone
briefings.message: Brandon Woodruff starts, with a pitch-count limit of 90 and expected innings of 5.7. Mix offspeed and breaking pitches to Ketel Marte rather than letting him sit on fastballs; use the changeup against Corbin Carroll, but his offspeed read is a small sample. Prefer breaking pitches to Ildemaro Vargas, whose breaking-ball read is also a small sample. Attack Geraldo Perdomo in the zone and keep Nolan Arenado’s contact down. In a close finish, preserve Trevor Megill, Abner Uribe and Grant Anderson for leverage; use middle relief and depth in less competitive situations.
reminders: Treat the Vargas and Carroll matchup cues as small-sample reads.
Use middle relief first in a blowout; preserve the leverage arms.
Shane Drohan is limited; use only if needed or for one batter.

briefings.headline: Execute the approved matchup plan; protect leverage arms
briefings.message: Keep the approved lineup, including Brice Turang and William Contreras despite rest suggestions; sitting them costs 1.51 and 0.74 win-probability points, respectively. Rodriguez is the high-confidence expected Arizona starter, with Michael Soroka the alternative. Woodruff’s varied approach targets Marte, Carroll and Vargas; note the small-sample pitch reads for Carroll and Vargas. Save Megill and the setup arms for tight finishes, using middle relief and depth in less competitive situations. Shane Drohan is limited after pitching yesterday; Jake Woodford is unavailable.
reminders: Use Blake Perkins as a late outfield glove for a lead.
Lockridge is the late speed option; use situationally.
Turang and Contreras are available; rest is suggested.
Rodriguez’s lefty split and several pitch-group reads are small samples.
